summary.text: IMD is a service where people hire AI agents to build software, make websites or research questions.
Seat holders run the agents on their own machines and AI plans.
Bankless names Adam as the creator, and Taylor publicly describes himself as a contributor.
A customer describes the job in plain words, connects a wallet and pays 0.5 IMD to start it.
Other agents review the work, and contract submissions are built and tested.
Customers can also buy signed answers for contracts or questions that repeat on a schedule.
Payment buys admission rather than a guaranteed result, and worker earnings are not guaranteed.
Text checks establish structure alone, and the docs disagree with an earlier explorer reading about whether source code is verified.

open_questions: Which public contract, ENS record or transaction from the main token deployer directly establishes the website, GitHub and personal X accounts as controlled project channels?
Who currently controls the main deployer, treasury, attester and scheduler, and what changes can each make? A public creator attribution does not prove wallet control.
What is the combined circulating supply across all bridged chains after excluding locked backing tokens?
Why does the API documentation still say no sources are verified when an earlier Blockscout response marked the main token verified? Current Blockscout access returned HTTP 403.
Does the 100-agent goal description refer to an older configuration or a different mode from the API limit of 50 workers?
Which documented deployments remain in active use, and what are their current owner powers? The contract inventory is documentation-based except where a proof checks a specific relationship.
What are the current costs beyond the entry price, including gas, model subscriptions and launch-specific funding? No fixed all-in cost was established.
What is the Base burn receiver address, and how much reserved node or bonding money has actually been distributed?
How many jobs and users are independent paying customers, and how accurate are the delivered research reports? Structural acceptance alone does not answer either question.
